issues: Dolphin body is filled with random dither/static noise rather than reading as a solid lit phosphor form; it looks like scattered pixels instead of a shaped creature.
No crisp rim-light outline on the dolphin, so the silhouette edges dissolve into the background and the form feels muddy.
Dorsal fin and pectoral fin are poorly defined; the tail fluke is recognizable but soft, weakening the anatomical read.
No visible persistence/afterglow trails behind the dolphin, so the leap feels frozen rather than in motion.
Bottom-right metadata text (154BPM / PHR / etc.) is comparatively bright and uses a cleaner font that slightly competes with the hierarchy and breaks the tiny 3x5 bitmap aesthetic.
Bloom sits on a noisy interior instead of hugging crisp edges, giving a grainy glow rather than the smooth OEL halo.
Water-surface lines are a touch too straight/uniform, reading as flat rules rather than elegant rippling surface.
suggestions: Render the dolphin as a filled silhouette with a bright 1px rim-light contour, then reduce interior dither density so the body reads as a solid glowing object with subtle internal shading.
Sharpen the anatomy: give the dorsal fin, pectoral fin, and tail fluke distinct outlined shapes so the silhouette is unmistakable at 320x128.
Add 2-3 short, decaying persistence ghosts trailing the dolphin's arc to convey the leap without fogging the scene.
Dim the bottom-right metadata and re-typeset it in the same 3x5 bitmap font as the top track text to keep it subordinate.
Concentrate bloom as a gentle halo around the crisp dolphin outline rather than as interior noise; keep peak brightness moderate to avoid a grainy whiteout.
Introduce slight amplitude variation and a faint second/third ripple row to the water lines so they feel like a living surface while staying low-contrast.
Verify the eye-path hierarchy by ensuring the dolphin's peak luminance clearly exceeds text, waves, and FFT in that order.
